$comment: Per-dialect capability descriptor. An agent reads this AFTER the http-mcp `transports` tool tells it MQTT is adapter-provided. Declares how this dialect maps down onto the wire's two atoms — honestly: the broker session is CHANNEL-shaped, but every atom this adapter puts on the wire is a CALL (http_request) to the witness.

maps_to.session: held broker connection, ADAPTER-INTERNAL — one TCP session per node, dialled OUT (no inbound port; sandbox-safe); the node produces into it (PUBLISH) and consumes from it (deliveries). It is never exposed upward as a bidi_command socket.
maps_to.commands: frames on the session — the far end publishes an envelope to <prefix>/commands/<ulid> (QoS 1) proposing ONE atom: a CALL (http_request shape) or a seat-addressed command ({session, method, params})
maps_to.fire: CALL (http_request) — the host fires EVERY envelope as an HTTP request to the witness: POST /fetch for a CALL, POST /run?session=<seat> for a seat-addressed command (the WITNESS holds the BiDi socket; the adapter never does)
maps_to.receipts: frames on the session — the host publishes a thick receipt, X-8-Witness inside, to <prefix>/receipts/<ulid> (QoS 1, RETAINED); the broker pushes it, so the far end needs no poll
maps_to.presence: frames on the session — <prefix>/presence/<node>, retained + last-will: the held connection made visible to the other side

capability_shaped: QoS 1 at-least-once (PUBACK) both ways; QoS 2 deliberately not offered — exactly-once belongs to the receipt (idempotent by ULID), not the transport
retain: receipts and presence are retained, so a far end that was away still finds its answer
persistent session (CleanSession=false) on the host: the broker queues commands while the host is down — store-and-forward without polling
keep-alive (PINGREQ/PINGRESP), last-will presence, username/password, TLS (mqtts://, CA file)
authority split: far end PROPOSES, host-side Policy DECIDES what fires (inbound) and what the receipt may carry back (egress); -policy is REQUIRED and a missing file is CLOSED (no AllowAll default)
inbound gate (internal/guard): request headers are an ALLOWLIST; URLs with userinfo or credential-named query params (?access_key=) are rejected structurally
auth_slot resolution host-side (-slots, never published, kept out of any git working tree) — no credential ever enters a topic

egress gate: receipts echo only ALLOWLISTED response headers (Content-Type, Content-Length, X-8-*); a slot-authenticated call publishes only the body's sha256 unless the policy opts in (egress.authenticated_body)
why_not_wire: A broker session is a held duplex connection, so the TRANSPORT is CHANNEL-shaped — but topics, QoS, retain, wills and persistent sessions are application delivery logic, not a transport shape, and the session itself is the adapter's, never presented upward as a bidi_command. What actually reaches the wire from this adapter is one http_request per envelope (POST /fetch or POST /run at the witness): at the wire, mqtt reduces to CALL, exactly like gitbroker. The difference from gitbroker is delivery, not atoms: a broker PUSHES, so the far end gets its receipt without polling and a command queues at the broker while the host is down. The earlier claim that this adapter's wire atom is bidi_command was an overclaim (#1145).

carries.call: http_request — fired by the host as a CALL to the witness, POST /fetch
carries.channel: a seat-addressed command {session, method, params} — fired by the host as a CALL to the witness, POST /run?session=<seat>; the witness's held BiDi socket does the channel work (the far end names a seat, never a ws_url, and this adapter never holds a bidi_command socket)

shape_proven_by: mqtt_test.go — both nodes dial out to a broker we own (broker.go, stdlib): a CALL envelope and a seat-addressed command envelope each round-trip far end → broker → host → witness stub (X-8-Witness stamped; every fire is an http_request to the stub) → retained receipt → far end; a command published while the host is DOWN is delivered when it returns (persistent session); a duplicate ULID is skipped; policy refuses and gates egress; will/retain/wildcard/QoS1 proven at the client layer. Security gate (#1145) proven: a missing policy is closed, a nil policy is closed, a Set-Cookie never enters the receipt, userinfo/?access_key=/X-Api-Key envelopes are refused before publish, a slot-authenticated body is digest-only unless opted in. Also `loopback mqtt`. Set MQTT_TEST_BROKER=mqtt://host:1883 to run the same round-trip against a real broker (mosquitto).
transport_shape: CHANNEL — a held duplex broker session per node (push delivery, retain, persistent session). This is the transport's shape and the adapter's delivery semantics; it is NOT a wire atom this adapter emits (see wire_atoms).
